text:
alex (SE): Heads-up: Acme POC hitting two blockers during observability setup. 1) Their exported logs to their S3 bucket are failing with AccessDenied. 2) Trace correlation mismatch: their trace IDs (eg client-7a9c) do not appear in our console; we only see internal request ids. Also intermittent 429s during concurrent replay. Can we triage?

maya (AE): I asked them to share bucket policy, KMS key id, and the role ARN we should expect to see. Waiting on that. They asked whether outbound egress charges apply if we write to their S3.

ryan (infra): quick checklist: validate S3 PutObject IAM for the exporter role, check KMS decrypt/GenerateDataKey permissions, confirm bucket policy allows PutObject from our account principal. Run these from our export runner host for repro: `aws s3api put-object --bucket <bucket> --key test.json --body /dev/null` and `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://token` (if you have ciphertext). Error responses will confirm.

alex (SE): customer provided a sanitized log: `{time: "2025-12-08T15:02:01Z", level: "error", msg: "s3 upload error", err: "AccessDenied", req: "rwd-req-0b3f"}`. They also pasted a trace snippet where their root id is `client-7a9c` but our span shows `rwd-req-0b3f` only.

jordy (ops): note: we intentionally rewrite the internal routing id. We have a mapping header but only populate it if the incoming header `X-Client-Trace-ID` is present. If clients don't pass it we won't match. Recommend asking them to pass `X-Client-Trace-ID`. Test with: `curl -H "X-Client-Trace-ID: client-7a9c" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat` and confirm logs show `client-7a9c`.

maya (AE): customer wants a temporary workaround because they're blocked for demo tomorrow. Any config flip we can do server-side to copy `rwd-req-...` back to the customer trace field?

ryan (infra): we can change exporter to include `external_trace_id = headers['X-Client-Trace-ID'] || metadata['incoming_request_id']` and also write `external_trace_id` to the span's tags and to exported logs. That requires a canary deploy. I'll stand up a short-lived canary and enable `trace_passthrough=true` in config.

jordy (ops): for 429s I see spikes in the ingress metrics at ~2025-12-08T15:00; they hit burst concurrency ~6x above the reserved throughput. We can temporarily raise the per-customer burst limit for the trial or enable early shedding. Also enable exporter queueing (SQS) to smooth exports.

alex (SE): maya please confirm contract egress terms. Maya, ping pricing if needed.

maya (AE): pricing check: for trial we absorb small diagnostic egress <= 5GB. Anything beyond a committed Dedicated plan incurs egress fees per GB. I'll confirm exact numbers in the next 30m.

export-bot: Deploy started: exporter-v2025-12-08-canary (id: c-deploy-112). Status: pending.

ryan (infra): action plan: 1) Join a short call with their infra to run `aws s3api head-object` and `aws kms get-key-policy` and attempt a controlled PutObject, 2) Flip `trace_passthrough=true` on canary to validate downstream mapping, 3) Enable SQS buffering and jittered retry for exporter: config snippet `batch.max_ms=25; retry.jitter=true; queue.type=sqs`.

alex (SE): they asked if we can provide a minimal KMS policy snippet they can apply to allow our exporter role to use their CMK. Can you paste that, ryan?

ryan (infra): paste (sanitized): `{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Sid":"AllowExportRole","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::REDACTED:role/redwood-exporter"},"Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey*"],"Resource":"*"}]}`. They must scope Resource/Condition to their key id and consider Grant tokens if needed.

maya (AE): I scheduled a support window at 15:30 PT and invited customer infra + their security lead. Also told them we will not enable persistent exports until KMS policy validated.

alex (SE): small note: customer is worried about log contents. Remind them we redact PII by default in exported logs and we can toggle retention. I've linked the redact policy doc in the shared drive.

jordy (ops): update: canary is healthy on a single host. After enabling `trace_passthrough` I see our exporter logs include `external_trace_id=client-7a9c` for the canary traffic. Next step: confirm S3 PUT success with their bucket policy change.

maya (AE): customer applied the policy change and re-ran the test -> they report "PutObject success". They still saw a few 429s but far less frequent.

alex (SE): great. Please add final steps to the ticket: 1) confirm pricing (maya), 2) finalize KMS policy snippet and SOC answers (jordy + me), 3) recommend production rollout path (ryan).

ryan (infra): I'll follow up with a short runbook on how to debug exporter access issues (head-object, kms get-key-policy, common bucket policy mistakes) and attach to the ticket.

maya (AE): confirmed pricing with billing: trial diagnostics covered up to 5GB egress; after that it's on customer per GB. Sent an email to the customer.

alex (SE): closing: exports validated after KMS policy fix, trace correlation fixed with `trace_passthrough` canary, 429s mitigated by temporary burst raise + SQS buffering. Will keep ticket open for production rollout notes. Thanks all. :rocket:
